appropriate: the double rule under the serif 'Clear Ledger' reads at once as a ledger's totals line, plain and Everyman; the 'one honest number' idea still needs a sentence
distinctive: a text serif in title case with a double underline stands apart from the rounded lowercase blue/green sans of Xero, FreeAgent and QuickBooks, but a double-underlined serif wordmark is a generic silhouette
simple: describable in one sentence (the name in a serif over a double rule), but the symbol shifts from 'CL' at 64 and 48 px to a lone 'C' at 32 px and below, two shapes to remember
legible: the wordmark reads cleanly at 256 and 128 px and the CL at 48 px; at 16 px the 'c' with its two rules is a tiny smudge and the rules near hairline weight, risky on the thermal printer
adaptable: black, reversed, one-colour 64 and 32 panels all hold; the green CL app tile and the tab favicon work, though the CL sits small within its tile
timeless: no trend shape: a book serif and a double rule would have read the same ten years ago; no 'avoid' item touched
universal: the mirrored and rotated-90 panels show only the reversed name, no secondary figure or reading
clear: unsearched: double-underlined serif wordmarks are common among small accountancy and bookkeeping firms, and other firms already trade as Clear Ledger; no specific near copy known
congruent: moss/sage green away from money green, plain text serif in title case, symmetric, static, framed by the rule all match; the stroke reads heavier than regular and the bracketed serifs sharper than the 'softened corners' target
system: horizontal lockup, CL symbol and C small tier are drawn and consistent in colour, but no stacked lockup appears and the symbol changes letter count between tiers, so the lockups feel uneven
